tutorial.title: Committee Management Tutorial
tutorial.subtitle: Learn how to manage committees, assign members, and maintain democratic governance

create.heading: Create a Committee
create.description: Follow these steps to create a new committee for your organization.
create.step1_text: Enter a meaningful committee name (e.g., 'Central Committee') and a unique code (e.g., 'NC-001') that identifies this committee.
create.step2_text: Choose from Central, Provincial, District, Ward, or specialized types like Youth Wing or Women Wing depending on your organizational structure.
create.step3_text: If your committee operates in a specific region, enter the geographic reference code (e.g., 'np.3.15' for Kathmandu District).
create.step4_text: Click 'Create Committee' to finalize. Your committee will be created and ready for member assignment.
create.pro_tip: Use consistent naming conventions like COMM-YEAR-ID for easy identification

edit.heading: Edit Committee Details
edit.description: Update committee information such as name and status after it has been created.
edit.step1_text: Go to the committee you want to edit and click the 'Edit' button in the dashboard.
edit.step2_text: Change the committee name if needed. This is useful when organizational structures evolve.
edit.step3_text: Set the committee to 'Active' or 'Inactive' to control whether it's participating in elections.
edit.step4_text: Click 'Update Committee' to apply all changes. Members will still remain assigned.

assign.heading: Assign Members to Committee
assign.description: Add organization members to committees with specific roles and nomination types.
assign.step1_text: Navigate to your committee dashboard and click the 'Add Member' button.
assign.step2_text: Use the search box to find members by name or email. The list shows members with their basic information.
assign.step3_text: Choose the member's role (using the numeric role path like 1.1, 1.2, etc.) and nomination type (Elected, Appointed, or Volunteered).
assign.step4_text: If the member was elected, enter the election date. Click 'Assign Member' to complete. The member now has an active role in the committee.

remove.heading: Remove Members from Committee
remove.description: Manage committee composition by removing members when their term ends or status changes.
remove.step1_text: In the committee dashboard, scroll to the 'Active Members' section to see all current members.
remove.step2_text: Find the member you want to remove in the members table. You can see their name, role, and join date.
remove.step3_text: Click the 'Remove' button next to the member's name. A confirmation dialog will appear to prevent accidental removals.
remove.step4_text: Click 'Yes, Remove' to confirm. The member is immediately removed from the committee, though the assignment record is preserved for audit purposes.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Can I have the same person in multiple committees?
faq.a1: Yes! A person can hold roles in multiple committees simultaneously. This is useful for organizations with overlapping governance structures.
faq.q2: What's the difference between Elected, Appointed, and Volunteered?
faq.a2: Elected members were chosen through a voting process. Appointed members were selected by leadership. Volunteered members offered their services.
faq.q3: Can I edit a member's role after assignment?
faq.a3: Currently, you need to remove the member and reassign them with the new role. This ensures clear audit trails.
faq.q4: What happens when a committee member's term ends?
faq.a4: Remove the member from the committee to deactivate their role. Their assignment history remains in the system for audit purposes.
faq.a5: Committees can be marked as Inactive rather than deleted, preserving all historical records for accountability.
faq.q6: What's the role path numbering system?
faq.a6: Role paths like 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 represent hierarchical positions. The structure depends on your committee's bylaws and organizational design.

tutorial.pro_tip_1: Use consistent committee codes (e.g., COMM-YEAR-ID) for easy identification
tutorial.pro_tip_2: Assign a committee secretary early to help coordinate activities
tutorial.pro_tip_3: Keep geographic references updated for regional committees
tutorial.warning_1: Committee assignments are audit-logged for transparency and accountability
tutorial.warning_2: Changing a committee's status affects election participation immediately
tutorial.note_1: All committee data is encrypted and isolated per organization
tutorial.note_2: Committee structure templates are available to match your bylaws
